why_angle: The cited desktop3dprinters.us list gives slot counts, nozzle count and chamber °C for 23 enclosed multi-material printers. It never says which filaments each 4-spool changer rejects (TPU, third-party carbon or glass fiber) or whether the box heats to dry. This page compares the QIDI Box, Creality CFS and Bambu AMS 2 Pro on those three points, using maker pages or a named retailer's copy of the maker table, and all prices are from today.

page.h1: Enclosed 3D printer with multiple filaments: what each filament changer can feed and dry
page.desc: Enclosed multicolor 3D printers compared on their 4-spool filament changers: which ones dry while printing, accept carbon or glass fiber, or reject TPU. Prices checked today.
page.answer: Short answer. For an enclosed 3D printer with multiple filaments, the multicolor pick is the QIDI Q2 with a QIDI Box: $677 together, a 65 °C active chamber, and a 4-spool box that dries at 65 °C while printing and feeds carbon- and glass-fiber filament. Creality's K2 CFS box only uses desiccant.

page.after:
What the differences mean

All prices are from the makers' US stores on 2026-11-14.

  • A Q2 with a QIDI Box costs $72 less than the K2 Pro Combo. $449 + $228 = $677, and $749 − $677 = $72.
  • The K2 Pro gives about 44% more build space. 300 × 300 × 300 mm = 27.0 L, and 270 × 270 × 256 mm = 18.7 L. 27.0 ÷ 18.7 = 1.44.
  • The bigger QIDI setups: Plus5 + Box = $699 + $228 = $927 for 30.7 L. Max4 + Box = $1,049 + $228 = $1,277 for 51.7 L.
  • Cost per liter of build space with a 4-spool changer: Q2 $677 ÷ 18.7 = $36/L. K2 Pro $749 ÷ 27.0 = $28/L. Plus5 $927 ÷ 30.7 = $30/L. K2 Plus $1,099 ÷ 42.9 = $26/L. Max4 $1,277 ÷ 51.7 = $25/L.
  • Chamber heat: the QIDI printers reach 65 °C and the Creality K2 Pro and K2 Plus reach 60 °C, so the QIDIs run 5 °C warmer for ABS and ASA.
  • Going past 4 filaments on QIDI: up to 4 boxes per printer gives 16 spools. Four boxes plus the expansion kit cost 4 × $228 + $39.99 = $951.99.

What each filament changer can't feed or dry

An enclosed printer handles multiple filaments through a 4-spool changer that sits beside it. The enclosure is what lets you print ABS, ASA, nylon and fiber-filled filaments, but each changer has its own list of filaments it refuses and its own way of keeping spools dry. Here is what the three common changers accept and how they dry.

ChangerPrintersFiber-filled filamentFlexible filamentDrying
QIDI BoxQ2, Q2C, Plus5, Max4 (sold separately)ABS-CF/GF, PLA-CF/GF, PETG-CF/GF, PET-CF/GF, PPS-CF. Not QIDI PAHT-CF.TPU 64D only. TPE, generic TPU and TPU 95A are refused.Heater up to 65 °C, running at the same time as printing
Creality CFSK2 Pro Combo, K2 Plus ComboPLA-CF (Creality store), PA-CF (Creality FAQ)No TPU of any kindDesiccant only, no heater
Bambu Lab AMS 2 ProP2S Combo, H2D AMS Combo; also fits the P1SOnly Bambu PLA-CF, PAHT-CF and PETG-CF. Other carbon- or glass-filled filaments are refused.Only Bambu 'TPU for AMS'. TPE, generic TPU and Bambu TPU 95A are refused.Heater up to 65 °C, but per its own table it cannot fully dry ABS, ASA, PET, PA, PC, PVA, BVOH, POM, HIPS or the Bambu CF grades

Fiber-filled filament from other brands. MatterHackers' copy of Bambu's AMS 2 Pro table rejects 'other filaments that contain carbon fiber or glass fiber', so a third-party PETG-CF or PA-CF has to bypass the AMS 2 Pro. The QIDI Box takes ABS-, PLA-, PETG-, PET-CF/GF and PPS-CF from any brand, and Creality's CFS takes PLA-CF and PA-CF.

Damp engineering filament. Creality's store lists the K2 Pro Combo's CFS with 'Drying Method: Desiccant'. It keeps dry spools dry but cannot dry a damp one, so ABS, ASA and nylon need a separate dryer before they go in. The QIDI Box heats to 65 °C during the print. That is the same ceiling at which Bambu's table says the AMS 2 Pro cannot fully dry ABS, ASA, PA or PC, so plan on a standalone dryer for nylon and PC on any of these.

Flexible filament. None of the three changers feeds standard TPU 95A. Creality's K2 Plus FAQ says to load TPU on the printer's own spool holder, and the same applies to the QIDI and Bambu machines. A multi-filament job can still mix one flexible spool with the boxed ones.

If you already own a Bambu P1S. MatterHackers' AMS compatibility guide lists the P1S as taking the AMS 2 Pro and AMS HT (up to 4 units in any mix, through an AMS Hub for more than one), with a separate power adapter for each AMS 2 Pro. Bambu's forum announcement says that adapter is needed for drying.

To add a changer to a QIDI printer, the {buy:qidi-box} already includes the upgrade kit when bought on its own, so no other part is needed for one box.

I could not open the project's category registry because local file access was blocked, so I used the live site's product list instead. On 2026-11-14 I read https://dealectric.com/dealectric-products.csv (all 4 chunks). Its category column has no '3d-printer-accessory' value. It does have '3d-printer', which qidi-q2, qidi-plus5 and qidi-max4 use, plus '3d-scanner' and 'build-plate', which is used only for BIQU build plates. '3d-printer' is the closest existing category for the QIDI Box, a filament-changer add-on for those three printers. A separate accessory category would need adding to the registry first. https://dealectric.com/data (read 2026-11-14) lists only 10 older categories, so I took the live product list as the current set.

Not changed, outside this fix: the qidi-box 'warranty' value ('1 year from the date you receive the printer...') conflicts with the draft's own unsourced entry, which says the QIDI warranty page was never opened, and none of the sources covers it.
